user.title: Connect to Blocky
user.description: Enter the address of the Blocky HTTP API. Blocky's API has no authentication, so keep its HTTP port reachable only from trusted hosts.

data_description.url: Scheme, host and port only, for example {example_url}. For the Blocky add-on use its internal hostname, such as {addon_url}.

error.invalid_url: Enter a URL with only a scheme (http or https), host and optional port. Credentials, paths and query strings are not allowed.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to Blocky at this address.
error.invalid_response: The server answered, but not like a Blocky API. Check the address and that Blocky is v0.35.0 or newer.

abort.already_configured: This Blocky instance is already configured.

disable_blocking.name: Pause blocking
disable_blocking.description: Pauses Blocky's blocking for a limited time. Blocking resumes on its own afterwards.

config_entry_id.name: Blocky instance
config_entry_id.description: Which Blocky instance to pause. Only needed when more than one is configured.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long to pause blocking, from 1 second to 24 hours.

groups.name: Groups
groups.description: Blocking groups to pause. Leave empty to pause all of them.

allow_domain.name: Allow domain
allow_domain.description: Adds a domain to an allow list. Blocky reloads its lists shortly afterwards.

config_entry_id.description: Only needed when more than one Blocky instance is configured.

domain.description: A domain name such as example.com, or with a leading wildcard where the list allows it.

block_domain.name: Block domain
block_domain.description: Adds a domain to a deny list. Blocky reloads its lists shortly afterwards.

rotate_list_token.name: Rotate list token

approve_request.name: Approve request
approve_request.description: Approves a request of an allowlist-only zone: the domain is added to an allow list of the zone. A request can be used once.

config_entry_id.name: Blocky instance
config_entry_id.description: Only needed when more than one Blocky instance is configured.

request_id.name: Request
request_id.description: The id of the request, from the new domain event or from the list of requests.

list.name: List
list.description: An allow list of the zone to add the domain to. Leave empty to use the first allow list of the zone.

reject_request.name: Reject request
reject_request.description: Rejects a request of an allowlist-only zone, which then never asks again for that client and domain. In a learning zone it dismisses the request. A request can be used once.

block_request.name: Block request
block_request.description: Blocks the domain of a request of a learning zone: it is added to the first deny list of the zone. A request can be used once.

get_requests.name: Get requests
get_requests.description: Returns the requests waiting for a decision and the phase of the clients of allowlist-only zones.

config_entry_id.name: Blocky instance
config_entry_id.description: Only needed when more than one Blocky instance is configured.

set_client_phase.name: Set client phase
set_client_phase.description: Sets the phase of a client of an allowlist-only zone. A learning client turns blocked domains into requests; a locked client only causes an event.

client.name: Client
client.description: The IP address of the client.

database.title: Query log database
database.description: Optional. Connect to the MySQL or MariaDB database Blocky writes its query log to. Use an account that can only read: an account with write privileges is refused. Leave the host empty to switch the query log off.

data_description.db_host: Hostname or IP address of the database server.
data_description.db_password: Enter it again whenever you change these settings.

list_networks.title: Clients that may download lists
list_networks.description: Say which clients may download the manual lists from Home Assistant. Blocky downloads each list from Home Assistant. Which lists exist, and the other settings, are in the Settings tab of the HA-Blocky card.

data_description.list_networks: Networks in CIDR notation. Only clients in them can download a list. The default is the network of Home Assistant apps (add-ons).

list_urls.title: List addresses for Blocky

zones.title: Zones
zones.description: A zone is a named group of client networks. It is only a record kept in Home Assistant, used to tell which policy applies to a client in the query log. Home Assistant never changes Blocky's configuration; use "Zone configuration for Blocky" to get a fragment to copy. Zones must not overlap.

data_description.zone: Choose a zone to change or delete, or add a new one.

zone_edit.title: Zone
zone_edit.description: Zone: {zone}. Clients in the networks below belong to this zone. Filter: filtered as usual with the linked lists. Learning: filtered as usual; meant for watching which domains the clients ask for. Allowlist only: the clients may reach only the domains on the linked allow lists, which must be lists without wildcards.

data_description.name: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, up to 32 characters. It cannot be changed later.
data_description.networks: Between 1 and 8 addresses or networks in CIDR notation, for example 192.0.2.0/24. A network that matches every address is not accepted.
data_description.mode: How the clients of this zone are meant to be treated in Blocky.
data_description.lists: Manual lists used by this zone. Allowlist only needs at least one allow list without wildcards.
data_description.delete: Tick to remove this zone. Nothing in Blocky changes.

zone_config.title: Zone configuration for Blocky
